appImageRuntime.description: Override the AppImage type2 runtime binary. Defaults to a pinned `fetchurl` of `AppImage/type2-runtime`.

appImageTerminal.description: If true, the AppImage's bundled `.desktop` sets `Terminal=true` (CLI tools).

appstream.description:
AppStream metainfo at `/usr/share/metainfo/<bundleId>.metainfo.xml`,
the listing GNOME Software, KDE Discover and Flathub show: id,
names, description (blank lines split paragraphs), license,
developer (`windows.publisher`'s default: `maintainer` without the
email), homepage, launchable desktop entry, release and screenshots.
Shipped by deb, rpm, archlinux, tar, flatpak and AppImage.

appstream.enable.description: Ship the metainfo file. Defaults to on when `desktopEntries` is non-empty.

appstream.metadataLicense.description: SPDX license of the metainfo file itself (`metadata_license`). Flathub accepts CC0-1.0, CC-BY-*, FSFAP and MIT.

appstream.releaseDate.description: Date of this `version` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Without it the metainfo lists no release, since AppStream needs one per release and a build has no reproducible "today".
appstream.releaseDate.type: null or string matching the pattern [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}

appstream.screenshots.description: Screenshots for software centers; the first is the default one.

archlinux.description: Settings for the `archlinux` format (binary pkg vs AUR layout).

archlinux.output.description:
Selects what the `archlinux` format emits:
- `pkg`  → only the binary `*.pkg.tar.zst` (install with `pacman -U`).
- `aur`  → only an AUR-pushable `PKGBUILD` + `.SRCINFO` + source tarball.
- `both` → both, with AUR layout under `aur/`.

autoDepends.description:
For linux package formats (`deb`, `rpm`, `archlinux`), scan the staged
binaries' `NEEDED` SONAMEs and add matching distro packages to the
manifest's `Depends` / `Requires` / `depends` field. The mapping table
ships with the library; user-supplied `info.depends.<distro>` always wins
— auto-detected entries are merged in addition, never replacing.

binDir.description: Subdir under `/opt/<name>/` where binaries land. Rarely needs changing.

bundleId.description:
Reverse-DNS app id: macOS `CFBundleIdentifier`, flatpak app id, icon
and MIME package name on linux, and the seed of the MSI `UpgradeCode`.
Defaults to `com.example.<name>` when null.

bundleLibs.description:
When `true` (the default), Linux package formats copy every
non-glibc runtime library out of the derivation's Nix closure
into `/opt/<name>/lib/` and rewrite the binaries' `RPATH` to
`$ORIGIN/../lib` so the bundled copies resolve first. The
produced bundles are self-contained at the cost of being large.

Set to `false` to ship the binaries naked: no `lib/` dir gets
copied, no `RPATH` rewrite happens, and the dynamic linker
resolves SONAMEs through the system loader cache. Pair with
`autoDepends = true` (or hand-rolled `info.depends.<distro>`)
so the produced `.deb` / `.rpm` / `PKGBUILD` declares the
runtime libs as install-time deps — the target distro's package
manager pulls them in alongside the binary.

Tarball / archive formats ignore this flag (they have no
manifest to declare deps with), so they still bundle.

depends.description: Per-format runtime dependencies surfaced in manifests.

depends.nsis.description: (reserved; not yet used by the NSIS format).

desktopEntries.description: Declarative XDG Desktop Entry definitions to ship on linux bundles. The first entry is also used as the AppImage top-level `.desktop`.

desktopEntries.*.actions.description: Context-menu actions. Each becomes a `[Desktop Action <key>]` section.

desktopEntries.*.actions.<name>.exec.description: Command-line executed when this action is selected.

desktopEntries.*.actions.<name>.icon.description: Optional icon name reference for this action.

desktopEntries.*.dbusActivatable.description: Whether the app can be activated via D-Bus.

desktopEntries.*.exec.description: Command-line. Becomes the `Exec=` field. Supports `%F %U %f %u` placeholders.

desktopEntries.*.extra.description: Arbitrary extra keys to embed in `[Desktop Entry]`.
desktopEntries.*.extra.type: attribute set of (string or boolean or signed integer or list of string)

desktopEntries.*.hidden.description: Mark as deleted at the user level.

desktopEntries.*.icon.description: Icon name reference (looked up via the icon theme).

desktopEntries.*.iconPath.description:
Optional filesystem path to an icon file to ship with the bundle.
When set, the file lands at `/usr/share/icons/hicolor/512x512/apps/<icon>.png`.
desktopEntries.*.iconPath.type: null or absolute path or string

desktopEntries.*.mimeTypes.description: MIME types handled by this entry. Becomes `MimeType=`.

desktopEntries.*.noDisplay.description: Hide the entry from menus while keeping it registered.

desktopEntries.*.prefersNonDefaultGPU.description: Hint that the app should run on the discrete GPU.

desktopEntries.*.singleMainWindow.description: Hint that the app has a single primary window.

desktopEntries.*.startupWMClass.description: WM_CLASS to associate this entry with its window.

desktopEntries.*.terminal.description: Whether the launcher should open a terminal first.

desktopEntries.*.tryExec.description: Path to a binary that must exist for the entry to be shown.

displayName.description:
Human-facing app name: the macOS `.app` bundle and `CFBundleName`,
the DMG volume, the Windows installer, Start menu shortcut and
"Apps & features" entry. Defaults to `name`, which keeps driving
every path, package name and registry key.

downloadUrl.description: Public URL where the tarball will be hosted. Embedded in the brew formula's `url`.

extraFiles.description:
Extra files dropped into the staged tree at fixed absolute paths.
Keys are the destination paths inside the installed package
(e.g. `/lib/udev/rules.d/61-myapp.rules`). Values are either a
Nix path / store path (copied verbatim) or an inline string
(written directly into the destination at build time).

Honoured by the linux installer formats (`deb`, `rpm`,
`archlinux`). Ignored by `appimage` / `flatpak` / `snap` (no
system install location) and by darwin/windows formats.

If any entry lands under `/lib/udev/rules.d/`,
`/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/`, or `/etc/udev/rules.d/`, the
post-install hook will additionally run `udevadm control
--reload-rules && udevadm trigger` (best-effort).
extraFiles.type: attribute set of (absolute path or string)

fileAssociations.description:
File types the app opens, so installed bundles show it under "Open
with" and claim the types it defines.

- linux: every MIME type joins `MimeType=` of the desktop entries that
  set no `mimeTypes` of their own (`%F` is appended to an `exec`
  without a field code), and exported types ship
  `/usr/share/mime/packages/<bundleId>.xml`.
- macOS `.app` (and dmg, pkg, productbuild): `CFBundleDocumentTypes`,
  plus `UTExportedTypeDeclarations` for exported types and
  `UTImportedTypeDeclarations` for other non-system ids.
- Windows (MSI, NSIS): one ProgID per association with
  `shell\open\command`, listed under `OpenWithProgids` of every
  extension, and the extension default when `rank = "owner"`.
  The ProgID is `id` for exported types, `<bundleId>.<first extension>`
  otherwise.

fileAssociations.*.conformsTo.description: macOS only: parent UTIs of a declared type (`UTTypeConformsTo`).

fileAssociations.*.exported.description:
The app defines this type. macOS gets a `UTExportedTypeDeclarations`
entry and Linux a shared-mime-info package declaring the MIME types
with their extension globs.

fileAssociations.*.extensions.description: File extensions without the leading dot.

fileAssociations.*.id.description:
Uniform Type Identifier on macOS and ProgID on Windows for an
exported type. Use the system UTI for well-known types
(`com.adobe.pdf`, `public.plain-text`). Required when `exported = true`.

fileAssociations.*.mimeTypes.description: MIME types of the type. Linux matches desktop entries to files by these.

fileAssociations.*.rank.description:
How strongly the app claims the type. macOS `LSHandlerRank`; on
Windows `owner` also makes the app the default handler of every
extension, the other ranks only add it to "Open with".

fileAssociations.*.role.description: Whether the app only opens (`viewer`) or also saves (`editor`) the type. macOS `CFBundleTypeRole`.

flatpak.description: Settings for the `flatpak` format (manifest + source layout).

flatpak.command.description: Name of the binary `flatpak run <appid>` invokes. Defaults to `info.name`.

flatpak.extraModules.description:
Extra `modules` entries appended to the generated manifest. Each
should be an attrset matching the flatpak-builder schema (raw YAML
struct: `{ name = ...; buildsystem = ...; sources = ...; }`).

flatpak.finishArgs.description:
Sandbox permission flags passed to `flatpak-builder` via the
manifest's `finish-args`. Tune for GUI vs CLI vs networked apps.

flatpak.sdk.description: SDK paired with `runtime` for the build step.

hostLibs.description:
Library name prefixes that Linux bundles never copy out of the Nix
closure; the target's own copies are used instead. A prefix
matches `<prefix>.so*`, `<prefix>-*.so*` and `<prefix>_*.so*`
(so `libxcb` also covers `libxcb-xkb`, `libX11` covers
`libX11-xcb`).

The defaults are libraries every desktop distro ships and whose
Nix builds break off-Nix: GPU driver loaders (glvnd, Vulkan,
GBM) and libraries that read config or data from compiled-in
store paths (fontconfig, xkbcommon, X11 locales, ALSA). Package
formats still declare them as dependencies through
`autoDepends`.

Applies wherever libs are bundled (`deb`/`rpm`/`archlinux` with
`bundleLibs`, `appimage`, archives, and the payload `flatpak` /
`snap` stage). Setting it replaces the default list; `[ ]` gives
a fully self-contained bundle.

icon.description:
Square PNG (1024 px recommended) every format derives its icon from:
freedesktop hicolor PNGs named after `bundleId` (and the default
`Icon=` of desktop entries, the AppImage `.DirIcon`, the snap icon),
the `.icns` of a `.app` (unless `macOsIcon` is set) and the `.ico`
of the NSIS / MSI installers and their shortcuts.

keepInterpreter.description: If true, do not rewrite the ELF dynamic loader path on linux bundles (advanced).

libDir.description: Subdir under `/opt/<name>/` where bundled libs land.

macos.description: macOS-only settings: the `.app` bundle's `Info.plist`, icon override and entitlements.

macos.buildVersion.description:
`CFBundleVersion`, the build number. Defaults to the numeric
`version`, which is always `CFBundleShortVersionString`.

macos.category.description: `LSApplicationCategoryType`: where Finder and the App Store file the app.

macos.copyright.description: `NSHumanReadableCopyright`, shown in the About window and in Finder.

macos.icns.description:
`.icns` that replaces the one rendered from `icon`. Copied into
`Contents/Resources/AppIcon.icns` and referenced by `CFBundleIconFile`.
macos.icns.type: null or absolute path or string

macos.infoPlist.description:
Extra `Info.plist` keys for anything without its own option. Applied
last, so they override generated keys. Values are strings, booleans,
integers, lists and attribute sets (dictionaries).

name.description: Package name. Drives install paths, manifest fields and output filenames.

permissions.description:
What the app needs from the system, declared once. Each format turns
it into its own form: usage descriptions in the macOS `Info.plist`.

permissions.network.local.description:
The app reaches devices on the local network: LAN broadcast or
multicast discovery, or connections to other hosts on the LAN.

- macOS bundles: `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` from `reason`.
- Windows (MSI, NSIS, per machine): an inbound firewall rule for
  `udp` / `tcp` ports, removed on uninstall.
- flatpak: `--share=network`; snap: `network`, plus `network-bind`
  when ports are declared.

permissions.network.local.reason.description:
Why the app talks to devices on the local network, shown in the
permission prompt. macOS (`NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`): without
it the system refuses LAN traffic without asking, and sockets fail
with "No route to host".

example.text: "Finds and streams from apps running on your network."

permissions.network.local.tcp.description: TCP ports the app listens on; like `udp`.
permissions.network.local.tcp.type: list of 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)

permissions.network.local.udp.description:
UDP ports the app receives on. Windows: the MSI and NSIS installers
add inbound firewall rules for them (machine-wide installs only),
so Defender neither blocks nor asks on first run.
permissions.network.local.udp.type: list of 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive)

productbuild.description:
Settings for the macOS `productbuild` distribution format. Drives the
welcome / license / readme / conclusion screens and the installer chrome.

productbuild.allowCustomize.description:
If true the installer offers the Customize button. Useful when the
distribution contains more than one component.

productbuild.background.type: null or absolute path or string

productbuild.conclusion.description: Path to a conclusion screen file shown after install completes.
productbuild.conclusion.type: null or absolute path or string

productbuild.license.description: Path to a license file shown on the License screen.
productbuild.license.type: null or absolute path or string

productbuild.readme.description: Path to a readme/release-notes file shown on the Readme screen.
productbuild.readme.type: null or absolute path or string

productbuild.title.description: Installer window title. Defaults to `info.name` when null.

productbuild.welcome.description: Path to a welcome screen file (rtf/rtfd/html/txt).
productbuild.welcome.type: null or absolute path or string

services.description:
Cross-OS background services. Materialised as systemd unit (`/lib/systemd/system/`)
on linux, launchd plist (`/Library/LaunchDaemons/`) on macOS `.pkg`, and
`sc.exe`-based registration via shipped batch files on Windows.

services.*.environment.type: attribute set of (string or signed integer)

services.*.launchd.label.description: Override the `Label` plist key. Defaults to the service `name`.

services.*.name.description: Service identifier (becomes systemd unit basename / launchd Label / sc.exe service name).

services.*.systemd.wantedBy.description: Targets that pull this unit in via `WantedBy=`.

services.*.windows.depends.description: Names of services this one depends on.

services.*.windows.serviceName.description: `sc.exe` service name. Defaults to the service `name`.

signing.description:
Codesigning hooks. Bundles always build unsigned; when an entry is
`enable = true` the corresponding format also drops a turnkey
`sign.sh` next to the artifact, ready to run with secrets supplied
via env vars (`P12_PASSWORD`, `PKCS12_PASSWORD`, `GPG_KEY_ID`).
See README "Codesigning" for the workflow.

signing.darwin.enable.description: Generate a `sign.sh` next to darwin artifacts that drives `rcodesign`.

signing.darwin.entitlements.type: null or absolute path or string

signing.darwin.hardenedRuntime.description: Set the hardened-runtime code-signature flag (`--code-signature-flags runtime`).

signing.darwin.p12File.description:
Path to a `.p12` developer-id signing identity. Can be a nix store
path (read at script-runtime) or an absolute host path. Override at
runtime via `P12_FILE=...` env var.
signing.darwin.p12File.type: null or absolute path or string

signing.darwin.teamId.description: Apple Team ID (10-char). Embedded as `--team-name`. Override via `TEAM_ID`.

signing.linux.description: Per-platform signing settings — linux (GPG / dpkg-sig / rpmsign).

signing.linux.enable.description: Generate a `sign.sh` next to linux artifacts that drives GPG / dpkg-sig / rpmsign.

signing.linux.keyId.description: GPG key fingerprint or short id used as `--local-user`. Override via `GPG_KEY_ID`.

signing.linux.style.description:
`detached` → emits `<artifact>.sig` next to the bundle (works for any format).
`embedded` → uses `dpkg-sig` (deb) or `rpmsign --addsign` (rpm) to embed
the signature inside the package. Ignored for appimage/archlinux/tar*.

signing.windows.description.description: Embedded `-n` description shown in signature properties.

signing.windows.enable.description: Generate a `sign.sh` next to windows artifacts that drives `osslsigncode`.

signing.windows.pkcs12File.description: Path to a `.pfx`/`.p12` Authenticode signing cert. Override via `PKCS12_FILE`.
signing.windows.pkcs12File.type: null or absolute path or string

signing.windows.url.description: Embedded `-i` URL shown in signature properties.

snap.description: Settings for the `snap` format (`snapcraft.yaml` + source layout).

snap.confinement.description: Sandbox confinement level. `classic` requires Snap Store review.

snap.grade.description: Snap grade (devel snaps may not be promoted past edge/beta).

summary.description: One-line summary (deb Description, rpm Summary, etc).

urlSchemes.description:
URL schemes the app handles (`hello://…` links). A plain string is
the scheme.

- linux: `x-scheme-handler/<scheme>` joins `MimeType=` of the desktop
  entries that set no `mimeTypes` of their own; an `exec` without a
  field code gets `%U`, so files arrive as `file://` URIs too.
- macOS `.app` (and dmg, pkg, productbuild): `CFBundleURLTypes`.
- Windows (MSI, NSIS): `Software\Classes\<scheme>` with
  `URL Protocol` and `shell\open\command` passing the URL as `%1`.
urlSchemes.type: list of ((submodule) or string convertible to it)

urlSchemes.*.name.description: What the scheme is, for the system's UI (`URL:<name>` on Windows). Defaults to `displayName`.

urlSchemes.*.scheme.description: URL scheme without `:` or `//`, e.g. `hello` for `hello://open?x=1`.

version.description: Semantic version. Appears in manifest fields and bundle filenames.

windows.description: Windows-only settings for the MSI and NSIS installers.

windows.arp.description:
Extra "Apps & features" (Add/Remove Programs) fields. `homepage`
already fills the about link.

windows.installDirName.description:
Install directory name: under `%ProgramFiles%`, or under
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` for a per-user install. Defaults to `name`.

windows.publisher.description:
Shown as the publisher in "Apps & features" and the MSI
`Manufacturer`. Defaults to `maintainer` without the `<email>`.

windows.scope.description:
`perMachine`: `%ProgramFiles%`, needs admin, for every user.
`perUser`: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, no admin prompt, for the
installing user only (firewall rules need admin, so none are added).

windows.upgradeCode.description:
Pinned `UpgradeCode` GUID for the MSI. Derived deterministically from
`bundleId` if null — **pin this once you cut a release**, otherwise
future MSIs won't be recognised as upgrades.
